newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 26.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Coalition parties are likely to favour Uthai Pimchaichon or Ukrit Mongkolnavin to chair the Constitution Drafting Assembly. Parliament convenes today to elect the 99, comprising one representative from the 76 provinces and 23 experts in law, political science and national administration. Its duty is to elect assembly members but the decision on who will be chairman rests with the elected members. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- The public and the media should be patient and give the new government time to do its job, says Deputy Prime Minister Amnuay Viravan. He has expressed confidence in Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh's sincerity and determination to systematically tackle problems that have dogged the country for a long time. (BANGKOK POST)

- Supreme Commander Mongkol Ampornpisit has resigned as chairman of the Mass Communication Organisation of Thailand's board of directors. Although General Mongkol says that he relinquishes the post voluntarily, speculation is that he was asked to do so by Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh. (THE NATION)

- The country's largest cement producer, Siam Cement, is to co-invest with Tirtamas of Indonesia in a project worth 80 billion baht to produce a full range of petrochemicals in Indonesia. The joint venture company, Trans-Pacific Petrochemical Indotama, will be set up withy Tirtamas, together with a Japanese and an American company in each part of the integrated petrochemical project. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Isuzu Motors plans to boost its export revenue generated from truck engines and body components 10 fold from 200 million baht this year to over two billion baht in 1998. The Japanese truck maker will push Thailand as its export hub for one-tonne pick up truck engines and body parts. (THE NATION)

- In a bid to stimulate the economy, the Commerce Ministry has removed price controls on automobiles with engines smaller than 1600cc. At the same time the Price Fixing and Anti-Monopoly Committee also votes to remove bottled drinking water from its list of controlled products. (BANGKOK POST)
